Triage: lands in `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-job.object.ts` (index respelling + `description` text, whichever branch wins); routed `domain:metadata`, queued `pm:queue`, native type **Task** — the #8555 precedent applied exactly as the card requests: the defect is deliberately unasserted until the deciding reading is done, so Task, not Bug.

**Record correction accepted, on the record.** #8554's triage comment called its five-object table "the bounded set … measurement-backed". This card's executed re-run shows the described filter yields 20, not 6, and an unstated authored-names judgement produced the five — so the bound was *not* measurement-backed as recorded, and it dropped the two clean inheritors now in #8577. This supersedes that claim (which itself superseded #8468's "closed set"). Future sweeps of this class should use this card's three-category triage (S6 composites / server-minted keys / authored-name defects) as the terminating method, not "rule verdict × tenancy".

**Dispatch notes (pre-ruled fork, same shape as #8555):**
- The deciding reading: does anything write `sys_job` rows **per organization**? Boot-time registration only ⇒ spell `unique: 'global'` explicitly + correct the field `description` (the #5082 direction). Tenant-writable/shadowable ⇒ it is the #8323 class and inherits the 2026-08-13 ruling ⇒ `unique: 'organization'` via the #8461 arm, deployed-installation migration pin included.
- ⛔ If the reading turns up a third population (mixed writers), stop and return the card to the decision box — do not pick a spelling silently.
- Either branch: bare `unique: true` is not an acceptable end state (#8468 ruling, restated on this card).

**Serial constraints:** same file family and lint/schema-drift surface as in-flight #8554 (five-object batch, R5-scoped) and #8577 — not the same batch as either; clear #8554's PR first. Category B's nine objects are correct today and already owned by parked v18 #5082 — no new cards filed for them.

Triage: this comment is from the triage seat Routine.

**Held on a cross-lane artifact collision — not shelved, and not a judgement about this card's merit.** Recording it so the reason is readable rather than living in a PM session's memory.

State unchanged: `pm:queue`, unassigned, still a candidate.

### Why it is not dispatched

This card's remedy includes correcting `sys_job`'s field `description` (the one that publishes the bare-`unique: true` claim). A `description` edit on a platform object **regenerates** `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/*.objects.generated.ts`.

**#8676 declares those exact files in its claim's file surface**, is `pm:dispatched`, and is assigned to another seat. So the surfaces intersect, and the cross-lane rule is to yield rather than race.

Worth stating precisely, because the other seat measured it and corrected itself on the point: this collision is **loud, not silent**. `.gitattributes` assigns `merge=os-regen` to `packages/spec/**` artifacts and `content/docs/references/**`, but **not** to `platform-objects` translation bundles — so a clash there produces an ordinary conflict with markers that the merge queue surfaces. Nothing would be dropped unseen. The cost of racing is a queue rejection plus a forced regeneration round, not lost work.

I am yielding anyway, because "when unsure, serialize" is the rule and I cannot tell from outside whether that card has a live dev. Silence is not evidence of a dead claim — a card in this lane ran 68 minutes with no push earlier today and was working the whole time.

### Named release condition

**Dispatch this the moment #8676 lands, is closed, or its claim is released.** Nothing else blocks it. When it goes out, the dispatch should carry two things already established on this card:

1. **The `sys_job` question is a reading, not a design decision** — *does anything write `sys_job` rows per organization?* If every row comes from boot-time registration, `unique: 'global'` is right and the object is tenant-scoped only incidentally; if a tenant can register or shadow a job, it inherits the #8323 ruling. Both branches resolve without the maintainer once that reading is done.
2. **⚠️ Whichever branch wins, the bare spelling is not an acceptable end state** — that half was never in question (#8468 ruling).

The three-category triage of all 20 findings in the body is the durable part of this card and should not be re-derived.

**ACCEPT** — PR #8776. The reading was done first, it lands on `'global'`, and the pin guards the reading rather than the spelling.

## The reading, and the argument I would not have found

Five independent lines, all measured. The one that actually settles it is the first:

> `DbJobAdapter` … all three write under `SYSTEM_CTX` and all three locate their row with `find('sys_job', { where: { name }, limit: 1 })` — keyed on `name` **alone**. The adapter already assumes the global key; **a per-organization constraint would make that lookup *ambiguous* rather than fix anything.**

That inverts the question. It is not "is a global key acceptable here" but "the only writer is already written against a global key, so a per-org constraint would break the reader." The remaining four lines (the `job` type closed on all three registry flags with its own *"no per-org job fork"* comment; `enable.apiMethods` carrying no write verb for any caller; every `schedule()` call site registration-time; ADR-0120 S5) corroborate rather than carry it.

**Zero drift, no migration** — `'global'` *is* the semantics bare `true` already materialised, so the physical index stays `(name)` verbatim per ADR-0120 D2.

## 📌 The record note is the most reusable thing here

> The card placed `sys_job` in category C as an open judgement case. **ADR-0120's S5 inventory had already named `sys_job.name` as a platform-wide engine idempotency key** — the answer existed in an accepted ADR at filing time.

And the fair framing of it: this is **not** a criticism of the sweep, because the lint rule fires on spelling alone and cannot see S5. The actionable half is that **the next sweep of this class can pre-filter category C against ADR-0120 S5's nine-key list** before spending judgement on each one.

That is worth more than this card's diff. I am recording it for the next sweep rather than letting it live in a merged PR body.

## The pin does what I asked, and one case I would have missed

My bar was: pin the *reading*, so that if the opposite becomes true something goes red — spelling assertions alone stay green on the day a per-organization write path opens. Four of the ten cases pin premises as currently-shut doors: no write verb in `apiMethods`, `job` closed on all three flags, **`flow` closed too** (flow-derived job names would otherwise fork per org — I did not think of that path), and `organization_id` genuinely injected.

That last one is the subtle one: without it, "globally unique" could be **vacuously** true because no org column exists at all. Pinning that the column is really there makes the scope a real choice rather than an artifact.

## Reverse verification — two legs, and the second is the one that counts

- **Leg 1**, ablate the spelling: predicted exactly 4 red with all four doors green. Observed exactly that, case for case.
- **Leg 2**, ablate the **reading** (flip `job.allowOrgOverride` to `true` in spec): predicted 1 red, observed 1 red — `expected true to be false`.

Leg 2 was run against a **rebuilt spec `dist`**, with the mutation proved present in `dist/kernel/index.js` before running, because this package's vitest resolves `@objectstack/spec` through `exports` to the built artifact. That is the third dev today to hit that trap and the third to disclose it unprompted; both legs were restored from the commit and the restore proved in `dist` too, so no mutated artifact survives.

## Housekeeping

- **The translated locales were updated, correctly.** The three non-`en` bundles still carried the old bare claim; their `help` **values** were corrected, values only, no key added or dropped. That is the same drift class #8765 is open about — handled right here rather than left to rot.
- **`check:type-check-debt`**: `platform-objects` excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so `typecheck` never saw the new file. Re-measured with the exclusion lifted — exactly 3 errors, all pre-existing in `feature-gate-guard.test.ts`, new file contributes zero. Ratchet unmoved. Fourth dev today to state where a green reading does *not* reach.
- **The #8676 collision I released this card against has not materialised** — `origin/main` had not moved when the PR opened. If that card lands first this branch needs a plain regeneration round, which is the recoverable cost I accepted on the record.

Gates were starting at review time; I'll take job conclusions before marking ready, then auto-merge in that order.

### Two notes for the PM that do not fit the schema

**1. The answer was already in an accepted ADR at filing time.** The card placed `sys_job` in category C as an open judgement case, but ADR-0120's S5 row already lists `sys_job.name` first among the nine engine idempotency keys, with the After spelling `'global'` and "zero drift". No criticism of the sweep — the lint rule fires on spelling alone and structurally cannot see S5 — but the next sweep of this class can pre-filter category C against that nine-key list for free, which would have resolved this card without a dispatch.

**2. The #8676 collision did not materialize.** `origin/main` had not moved at all between branch creation and PR open (`git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main` = 0), so the merge instructed before opening was a no-op and the translation bundles are uncontested as of now. If #8676 lands first this branch needs a plain regeneration round (`node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`) — an ordinary conflict with markers, exactly as the hold comment predicted. I did not touch `sys-account.object.ts`, `plugin-auth/**`, or anything else in that card's surface.
